objective: New usernames follow the human's rule (ADR 0035): 1 to 30 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and dots, starting with a letter, digit or underscore, with no two dots in a row and no trailing dot. POST /users enforces it with one clear 422 on username; existing names that break it are grandfathered (every read and every other write still accepts them, and nobody is renamed).
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: this spec's Director PR has merged into the integration branch outstanding-track-4, and the unit's branch agent/USERS-010 is cut from its tip.
Test-first: commit the failing tests alone before the implementation. They fail today because CreateUserRequest.username is a bare str that accepts every value.

The rule is the pattern ^(?!.*\.\.)(?!.*\.$)\w[\w.]{0,29}$ compiled once at module level with re.ASCII and applied with fullmatch (no re.MULTILINE, no search/match). It lives in app/users/schemas.py as a field_validator on CreateUserRequest.username, not as Field(pattern=...): pydantic's default Rust regex engine has no lookaround.
Accepted by POST /users (201, stored exactly as sent, no case folding, ADR 0010): a, _, 9, raptors_fan, Raptors.Fan, a.b.c, a 30-character name, 1a, _a.

Rejected by POST /users with 422 before create_user runs, detail[].loc ending in username: an empty string, a 31-character name, a leading dot (.a), a trailing dot (a.), two dots (a..b), a hyphen (a-b), a space (a b), an @ (a@b), a non-ASCII letter (élise, ıllini with a dotless i), a full-width letter, a trailing newline (abc followed by a newline), an embedded newline (abc, newline, def), a leading or trailing space. No row is written for any of them.

The 422's msg for a username that breaks the rule is exactly: Use 1 to 30 letters, numbers, underscores or dots, with no two dots in a row and no dot at the end. Raised as pydantic_core.PydanticCustomError (type username_format) so the msg carries no 'Value error, ' prefix; the frontend shows it verbatim (FRONTEND-050).

Grandfathering: PublicUserOut.username and MeOut.username stay bare str. A User row whose username breaks the rule (inserted directly, as an old row would be) is returned unchanged by GET /users/{id} and GET /users/me, appears in GET /search/accounts and in feed PostView.author.username, can still PATCH /users/me (username is not a field of UpdateMeRequest and stays that way), follow and be followed. No migration, no CHECK constraint, no backfill, no rename.
Uniqueness and case are unchanged: the existing case-sensitive UNIQUE(username) stays the only uniqueness rule, and a duplicate still answers the existing generic 409.

Proof: CI's backend-test (the gate job) is green; ruff and mypy are clean. backend/openapi.json is regenerated and committed if the schema output changed (a field_validator alone does not change it; if it is unchanged, say so in the PR).
No new dependency, no Alembic revision, no change outside the allowed paths.
wiki/CodeContext/Modules/0x01c-users-routes.md states the rule, where it is enforced, the exact 422 msg and the grandfathering, in the POST /users bullet.
